findings.title: totalPages over-counts by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
findings.body: `totalPages` is `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. With 50 members and limit 50 it returns 2 although there is only one page. `showingLast` (`currentPage == totalPages`) stays false, so the 'next' arrow is enabled. Clicking it requests offset 50 and shows an empty page labelled 2/2. The same happens in the admin UI after removing the only member on the last page. `findMembers` clamps the offset using the stale `user_count`, so it requests an offset equal to the new total and lands on an empty page. This should be `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`.

findings.title: limit/offset are taken from params without bounds or validation
findings.body: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` are used directly in the query. There is no upper cap, so `?limit=1000000` serializes every member of a large group in one request. A negative limit or offset is passed to SQL and raises a Postgres error, giving a 500. The limit should be clamped to a sane range (for example 1..N) and the offset to >= 0.

findings.title: Public group members page now shows only the first 50 members with no pagination
findings.body: `GroupsController#members` now applies limit/offset to every group and defaults to 50. Before, the default limit only applied to automatic groups and non-automatic groups returned all members. `group-members` route and `group/members.hbs` were changed to call `findMembers()` once and render `members`, but only the admin template got next/previous controls. For any group with more than 50 members, the public page silently truncates the list and offers no way to see the rest. The JSON response shape also changed from a bare array to `{members, meta}`, which breaks any other consumer of this endpoint.

findings.title: findMembers returns undefined for nameless groups and no longer resolves to the member list
findings.body: `findMembers` used to always return a promise (`Ember.RSVP.resolve([])` for an empty name) that resolved to the members. Now it returns `undefined` when the name is empty, and otherwise a promise resolving to `undefined` because it writes into the model. Any caller that chains `.then(...)` on the result will throw for nameless groups, and callers expecting the members from the promise get nothing.

findings.title: `usernames` input state is never reset, so it leaks between groups and repeat clicks
findings.body: `usernames` lives on the singleton controller and is neither cleared after `addMembers` (only a TODO) nor reset in the route's `setupController`. Names typed for group A and not submitted stay in the selector after navigating to group B, and clicking Add there adds them to B. Clicking Add twice also resubmits the same names. `addMembers` also has no failure handler, so a server error is swallowed silently.

findings.title: remove_member spec uses PUT while the route is DELETE
findings.body: The route is `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`, but the 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' test calls `xhr :put, :remove_member`. It only passes because Rails 4 controller specs do not enforce the HTTP verb, so the test does not exercise the real request.

findings.title: No spec covers the changed GroupsController#members contract
findings.body: `GroupsController#members` changed its response from a bare array to `{members, meta: {total, limit, offset}}`, and the default limit/offset behaviour changed. No spec was added or updated for this (groups_controller_spec is not in the change). Pagination, the meta values, and the new response shape are untested, and any existing spec asserting an array response would now fail.
